video_caption: The video opens with a black screen featuring a faint white horizontal bar in the center, above a blurry, white, broken line of text. This quickly transitions to a vibrant lime green background, where a stylized, dark green and black profile image of a man, from the neck up, facing left, is displayed. Overlaying this image, in white text, is the logo "MMH" on the left, connected by a spiky, star-like shape near the man's ear to "MUSEUM OF MEDIA HISTORY" on the right. Below this, also in white, is "SPECIAL PROJECTS DIVISION" underlined, followed by "Tampa Bay Federal District, Florida". The scene then cuts back to a black screen, where a small, bright white dot emerges in the center, rapidly expanding into a dynamic, spiky, star-like burst of white light. This burst gradually begins to shrink and dissipate, changing from bright white to a muted gray, eventually fading completely into the black background by the end of the segment.

The video begins with a black screen for a few seconds. At the 0:05 mark, a black and white image appears, showing a middle-aged man with short, light hair, wearing a dark suit and a patterned tie, looking directly at the camera with a calm expression. The background is blurred, hinting at an office or public setting with other indistinct figures. This image transitions back to a black screen at 0:14. Two seconds later, at 0:16, the white text "amazon.com" appears centered on a black background, with a white, upward-curving arrow connecting the 'a' to the 'z' beneath the text, resembling a smile. This logo remains on screen until 0:33, after which the screen is black again. From 0:36, the word "Google" appears in a stylized dark gray font, almost blending into the black background, centered on the screen.

The video opens with a stylized, gray, somewhat distorted "Google" logo on a black background. This logo then quickly fades out and reappears larger, overlaid on a black background filled with white text representing search results related to "Google." Some visible search results include "Danno Fireball. Writing for Google," "Google - Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia," "Google files for its long awaited IPO - Apr 30, 2004," "Google News Canada," "Church v. Google - How the Church of Scientology is forcing Google to censor its critics...," and a Japanese result reading "サイトの登録 / 削除" (Saito no tōroku / sakujo), meaning "Site registration / deletion." Both the Google logo and the search results then fade out, leaving a black screen. A moment later, a pixelated, white television-shaped logo with two antennas appears against the black background. Inside the television screen, the black text "TiVo" is visible, along with a simple black smiley face beneath it. This TiVo logo slowly zooms in until the end of the segment.

The video begins with a white rectangular logo centered against a black background, featuring a gray square with a black stylized "b" symbol inside, followed by the word "Blogger" in black sans-serif font. This logo quickly disappears, and then a new, slightly tilted gray rectangular logo emerges from the right side of the screen against the black background. This logo prominently displays a black smiley face icon on the left, followed by the word "friendster" in a black, sans-serif font. The "friendster" logo remains visible for the remainder of the segment.

The video segment displays a black and white screenshot of the Google News Beta homepage. The header features the "Google News BETA" logo, with navigation links including "Web," "Images," "Groups," "News," and "Froogle." A search bar is visible with "Search News" and "Search the" buttons, along with the text "Search and browse 4,500 news sources updated continuously." On the left sidebar, categories like "Top Stories," "World," "U.S.," "Business," "Sci/Tech," "Sports," "Entertainment," "Health," "Make Google News Your Homepage," and "News Alerts" are listed. The main content area highlights "Top Stories," with the prominent headline "Iraq Resolution Gives Wide Powers to US Forces," attributed to Reuters and published "35 minutes ago." A summary describes the UN, US, and Britain's request for UN endorsement of a power handover to an interim Iraqi government, with related articles from Forbes, Los Angeles Times, Xinhua, Christian Science Monitor, MLive.com, and New York Times, and "751 related" links. A small, pixelated image labeled "Europolitix" accompanies this article. On the right, other headlines include "Oil Price Settles at New $41.72," "Microsoft's Trial Against Go Forward," "Despite sore back, Casse practice," and "Moore Film Is Held Up By About Rights," each with related links. Below the main top story, another headline reads "Israelis: IDF forces out of Rafah camp" from CNN, "25 minutes ago," with a snippet about Israeli military officials and a small image labeled "TIME." At the 0:09 mark, the entire screen abruptly distorts and glitches into a pixelated, abstract pattern of black and white blocks, making all text and images unreadable for the remainder of the segment.

The video opens with a stark black background featuring the word "Google" in white, rendered in a slightly hand-drawn or distressed font. The text remains static for a few seconds before the entire screen fades to black, completely obscuring the "Google" logo.

The video opens with the year "2004" displayed in bright green against a black background, then transitions to a black-and-white image of a "Reason" magazine cover with the tagline "Free Minds and Free Markets." The cover features a circular, abstract, satellite-like image and text below reading: "NICK GILLESPIE... THEY KNOW WHERE YOU ARE! The unsung benefits of a database nation (see next page)," along with a small "$5.99 U.S. $6.99 Canada June 2004" on the side. This is followed by a grainy, black-and-white close-up of an electronic paper device with the "SONY" logo visible at the top and multiple lines of Japanese text displayed on its screen. The scene then shifts to a black-and-white rendering of the "Gmail" login page, showing "Gmail by Google BETA" and "Welcome to Gmail," detailing features like "Search, don't sort," "1000 megabytes of free storage," and "Keep it all in context," alongside a sign-in form. Next, a black-and-white screenshot of an "msn • Newsbot (beta)" webpage appears, displaying a news article profile for "George Tenet" dated "03.06.04," featuring a photo of two men in suits, and a sidebar titled "The Daily Me" with various news headlines. This transitions to a black screen with white static, revealing the "Beta A9" (Amazon's search engine) logo with a "Search:" bar. The word "Google" then appears in a stylized white font on a black background, followed by a brief, glitchy visual of abstract white shapes on black before fading out. Finally, the year "2005" flashes in green, leading to the "Microsoft" logo displayed in gray against a black background.

The video segment opens with the word "Microsoft" (Microsoft) in stylized, light gray italic text on a black background, which then quickly transitions to a glitchy, pixelated white text that is difficult to decipher, but appears to be "Friendster", accompanied by flickering white lines. The screen then goes black before displaying the year "2006" in white text. This is followed by a series of text overlays listing Google services: "Google combines all of its services: Tivo, Blogger, Gmail, Google News, and all of its searches into the Google Grid." As the text for "Google Grid" appears, a minimalist 3D grid structure, composed of white lines forming a 4x4 array of cubes, rotates and solidifies on the black background. The grid then fades and is replaced by the words "Google GRID" in white, stylized text with a streaky effect, reminiscent of speed lines. Finally, a 5x5 white grid on a black background fills the screen, with the words "STORE" and "PUBLISH" visible in two of its cells, as a white mouse pointer (shaped like a hand with a pointing finger) moves to hover over the "STORE" cell.

The video begins with the text "Google GRID" (Google GRID) in stylized white serif font on a black background, with a bright white glow behind and emanating from the letters, creating streaks that move from the bottom-left to the top-right. This logo then fades out, leaving a black screen. After a brief moment, the text "msn. Newsbotster" appears in a white sans-serif font on a black background, with a stylized butterfly symbol replacing the dot in "msn.". This logo remains on screen as a background of news headlines, in white text on a dark gray, grainy background, slides up. Visible headlines include: "Blair and Bush appeal to Nato," "'Rotten job can cause early death'," "Some Oppose Bush's Mideast Teacher Plan," "Programmers unite How the European elections could impact the software we use," and "U.S. Military to Allow ICRC to Visit Afghan Jail." There's also "Get more personalized news | Your History" and "The Daily We" along with "Livingstone looks to black voters" and "Credit rules shake-up unveiled" partially visible. The news feed background then fades away, leaving only the "msn. Newsbotster" logo. A rapid, streaky white flash briefly covers the screen before revealing the "msn. Newsbotster" logo again, which then fades to black.

The video opens with a black screen as a narrator speaks. At the 0:07 mark, a white, metallic-textured logo for "Googlezon" appears on the black background, featuring the Google font and the Amazon arrow-smile logo as the "z" in "Googlezon". This transitions to the "amazon.com" logo at 0:13, also in white on a black background, before reverting to the "Googlezon" logo at 0:15. The "Googlezon" logo then distorts into a white blur and flashes at 0:20, revealing a textured, metallic-gray rectangular card on a black background. The card progressively displays personal and demographic information: "G179-3219-0062", "WSMITH@GOOGLEZON.NET", "WINSTON SMITH", "500 3RD ST S", "ST. PETERSBURG, FL 33705", "BIRTH DATE 12-19-1979", "SEX M", "HGT 6-03", "CREDIT VISA (A)", "SOCIAL NETS JOURNALISTS, BOHOS, GAMERS", "DEMO CONSUMER++, MEDIAN INC., LIBERAL", and "10% OFF BOOKS, VIDGAMES, SOFTWARE". A black and white photograph of a bald man with a stern expression appears on the left side of the card, labeled "Preferred Customer". The card also shows "ISSUED 05-28-2006" and "EXPIRES 12-19-2012". The text details a user's personal data, consumption habits, and interests, implying a highly customized profile for targeted advertising and content, fitting the context of a merged Google and Amazon entity. The card then disappears, leaving a black screen until the video ends.

The video opens with the year "2010" displayed in a bold, bright green font against a black background, which then fades to black. Following this, numerous lines of white computer code scroll diagonally across the screen, mimicking data streams. Overlaid on this code, various white text snippets appear and scroll, resembling news articles or quotes, such as "To win the X Prize, SpaceShipOne will have to travel 62 miles up twice in two weeks with three people aboard" and "We encourage people to come out and bring their children, so their children can tell their children that they were there," illustrating the dynamic news generation mentioned in the audio. These text elements and the code then fade out, leaving a black screen again. Finally, the word "Microsoft" appears in a stylized, italicized dark gray font, subtly brightening to white before fading back to dark gray and disappearing, all against the black background, suggesting a competitive or reactive context related to the preceding narrative.

The video segment opens on a black background displaying stylized gray text: "The New York Times" at the top, "v." (meaning 'versus') in the middle, and "Googlezon" at the bottom, where the Amazon smile logo is integrated into the "zon" part of the word. This text implies a legal conflict between the two entities. After a brief moment, the screen transitions abruptly with a radial blur effect to a stark black and white image of the United States Supreme Court building, featuring its grand columns and steps, with the sky appearing completely black.

The video begins with a black screen on which the bright green numbers "2014" appear, centered. As a voiceover says "2014," the text slowly darkens to a forest green before fading out completely to black. Immediately after, the word "EPIC" appears in white, centered, with a mirrored reflection below it, both of which then gradually fade to a medium gray. The voiceover states, "Google's On unleashes EPIC." Finally, the "EPIC" text and its reflection fade out entirely, leaving a black screen.

The video opens with the word "epic" in a white sans-serif font centered on a black background, accompanied by a grey, reflected version of the word below it. Below "epic," the text "Evolving Personalized Information Construct" appears in white, then fades to a darker grey, and eventually disappears. A male voice narrates, explaining that this "Evolving Personalized Information Construct" is the system by which the "sprawling, chaotic mediascape is filtered, ordered, and delivered." Following this, the scene transitions to a black and white world map, initially dark, with faint grey outlines of continents. Gradually, bright white, star-like bursts of light begin to emanate from various points across the map, particularly concentrated in areas corresponding to continents like South America, Africa, Europe, Asia, and North America. These light bursts expand and spread, making more of the map glow white, visually representing the global dissemination and aggregation of information. The narration continues to explain that "everyone contributes now," from "blog entries to phone-cam images to video reports to full investigations," and that many contributors receive a "tiny cut of Google's immense advertising revenue, proportional to the popularity of their contributions," as the bright points of light continue to proliferate and intensify across the world map.

The video opens with a grayscale aerial view, likely of a landscape, featuring a mosaic pattern of dark, irregular shapes (possibly cultivated fields or forested areas) interspersed with lighter, irregularly shaped sections that could be open land, roads, or less vegetated terrain. This scene gradually fades to black by 00:10. The screen remains completely black for a few seconds before a small, white, star-like burst of light appears in the center at 00:14, pulsing and briefly expanding. Around 00:22, this star-like burst shrinks and moves to the left side of the screen, while a second, larger, more abstract white shape, resembling a figure with outstretched arms, emerges on the right. Both white shapes continue to pulse with light against the black background until the end of the segment.

The video begins with the word "ePIC" displayed in light gray on a black background, with a slightly darker, distorted reflection beneath it, as if on water. As a male voice speaks in the background, the reflection of "ePIC" gradually darkens from 00:09 to 00:25, becoming almost indistinguishable from the black background. Simultaneously, the top "ePIC" also slowly fades. By 00:30, both the word and its reflection have completely disappeared, leaving a solid black screen for the remainder of the segment.

The video segment opens with a black background featuring a white, gothic-style partial logo that reads "The New York Times" from 00:05 to 00:13. The screen then goes completely black until 00:27 when it transitions to a solid lime green background. Centered on this green background, white text appears: "© 2014 MUSEUM OF MEDIA HISTORY" (© 2014 MUSEUM OF MEDIA HISTORY), indicating a copyright notice from the Museum of Media History. After a brief return to a black screen at 00:39, the lime green background reappears at 00:41, now with subtle horizontal scan lines, creating a retro computer monitor effect. More white text, resembling old computer font, is displayed, listing credits: "Written by Robin Sloan and Matt Thompson," "Narration by Matt Thompson," "Music by Minus Kelvin," and "Flash production by Robin Sloan."
